actual_cues.text: The Unit app keeps a vehicle or operational team in view
while you work its calls.
Here, the Calls screen shows Ambulance Sixty-one and No Active Call.
The roles card reads zero of one, so this recording does
not establish a staffed crew.
Use the circular plus button at the lower right to open a new call when your
department permits you to create one.
In New Call, enter a clear Name and a useful Nature description.
Our example is explicitly labeled training only and describes a software exercise.
Review Priority and Type; this practice call uses Routine and Investigation.
Use Note for additional context that belongs with the call.
Choose names and classifications that make sense to your own
operation rather than copying a firehouse example into live work.
Call Location provides Address, GPS Coordinates, what3words and Plus Code
fields, along with Select Location on Map.
Destination POI is a separate choice and currently reads No destination selected.
This software-only exercise leaves the location and contact inputs empty; a real
assignment needs the location information required by your operating procedure.
A visible location field does not establish that a device has
supplied GPS coordinates or that an address lookup has succeeded.
In Select Dispatch Recipients, review individual users as well
as the broad Everyone option.
Wallace Boden is checked here, while Everyone remains unchecked.
In the Units section, Ambulance Sixty-one is also selected, bringing
this exercise to two selected recipients.
Confirm retains that reviewed audience; it does not demonstrate that a
recipient has received a notification.
Back on New Call, verify Dispatch To and its two selected recipients.
Dispatch Time is blank in this exercise; no future schedule is entered.
After reviewing the form, use Create once.
The Calls list now contains the new training exercise with Boden and
Ambulance Sixty-one shown on its card.
Open the training call and check its identity in Call Details.
This saved exercise has a department call number ending in eight, and
its Info view retains Routine, Investigation and the original note.
Choose Set Active for the incident you intend to work.
The app reports Call set as active and opens Select Status.
Select Status is the first of three steps.
The configured choices include Responding, Available, Committed, On Scene,
Staging, Returning and Out of Service.
Here, Responding is selected; use Next to review its destination.
Select Destination for Responding distinguishes Calls, Stations
and POIs from No Destination.
The selected row is our new training incident, ending in eight.
labels_to_check_in_actual_source: FD51-2026-0008 - TRAINING ONLY - Native Unit response and deselection

actual_cues.text: Check that identity before using Next, so the status update is
associated with the intended call.
Add Note shows the selected Responding status and the training call together.
The optional note makes clear that this is a software exercise.
Review the summary, then use Submit to save the update.
Status saved successfully is the returned result from that submission.
Back in Calls, the sidebar now shows Responding and the selected training call.
Keep the unit identity, its status and the active call in view when changing tasks.
The circle with an X below the active-call card is the Deselect control.
Deselect Active Call asks whether to deselect the current active call.
labels_to_check_in_actual_source: Are you sure you want to deselect the current active call?

actual_cues.text: Use Cancel to keep the selection or Confirm to clear it.
After Confirm, the sidebar reads No Active Call, while the incident remains in Calls
and the unit still reads Responding.
Clearing your active selection and closing the department
incident are separate operations.
Reopen the same training incident from Calls and confirm
its title in Call Details.
The three-dot menu at the upper right opens the available incident actions.
Edit Call and Close Call are separate choices.
Choose Close Call only when you have the authority and the
incident is ready for closeout.
The Close Call sheet requires a Close Type and provides a Close Note.
Notify everyone on the call is enabled in this recorded starting state.
Review that setting explicitly because the sheet describes alerting
the dispatched personnel, groups, roles, units and command team.
Close Type offers Closed, Cancelled, Unfounded, Founded,
Minor, Transferred and False Alarm.
Our example selects Closed and enters a Close Note explaining that
the software workflow is complete.
Notify everyone on the call is off for this local exercise.
Check the call identity and closeout information, then use
the green Close Call button once.
The app returns Call closed successfully and shows No Active Call.
The three earlier training calls remain listed, and this immediate view still
shows the cached Responding status.
A fresh app readback shows Released, No Active Call and the
original three training incidents.
Released is the observed final status here; it should not be
described as an Available selection or evidence of physical readiness.
Use these same identity, selection and closeout checks for a community
paramedicine car, a mental health response team, a search and rescue
vehicle, a security patrol, a wildland crew or an industrial response unit.
The names in this example are fictional training data; choose
the statuses, audience and incident details that fit your department.
